summary: Lucian Scherman worked in Indology. He studied at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1883–1887) and later held a post there from ~1893 to 1936.

Luciano Petech specialized in Tibetology and history/archaeology, having studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He held posts at Allahabad, Naples, Rome, and the Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente, and served as President of the IATS (~1989–1995).

Lucy Annette Jones is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University, studying under supervisors Anne Carolyn Klein and Edith Wyschogrod, and also studied under Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche (1996–1997).

Ludo Rocher was an Indologist who completed his degrees at Ghent University (~1944–1950). He held posts at the Free University of Brussels (~1951–1966) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1966–2016), serving as Professor of Sanskrit and Emeritus Professor.

Ludwig Alsdorf was an Indologist who studied at Hamburg under Walther Schubring (~1924–1928) and in Berlin under Heinrich Lüders (~1930–1935). He later succeeded Schubring in 1950, holding the chair at the University of Hamburg.
Ludwig Heller was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1888–1894). He subsequently held a post at the University of Greifswald from ~1896 to 1935.

Ludwig Lange was a linguist and historian who studied at Göttingen (under Theodor Benfey) and Leipzig. He held posts at Göttingen (~1849–1853), Charles University (~1853–1859), University of Giessen (~1859–1871), and Leipzig University (~1871–1885).

Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at TU Berlin, Manchester, and Cambridge. He held academic posts at Trinity College, Cambridge (1929–1947) and the University of Cambridge (1939–1947).
Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer. He later served as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.

Luigi Suali worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Bologna (~1899–1904) and under Hermann Jacobi (~1905–1907), and later held a post at the University of Pavia from ~1909 to 1951.

Luis Oscar Gómez worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his PhD at Yale under Stanley Insler. He held long-term professorships at the University of Michigan (~1973–2010) and served as Academic Director at Mangalam Research Center (~2010–2017).

Luise Hercus was an Indologist and linguist who studied at St Anne's College and the Australian National University. She served as a Reader in ANU's Department of South Asian and Buddhist Studies from ~1969 to 1991.
Lungten Dubgyur works in Tibetology and other fields. He completed degrees at Sherubtse College, Government Law College in Mumbai (LL.B), and the University of Edinburgh (LL.M).
Lungtok Tenpai Nyima was a figure in Tibetology and religious studies. He founded Menri Monastery and served as its abbot and throne-holder from ~1969 to 2017.

Lynn A. Struve is a scholar of Sinology and history. She studied at the University of Washington (~1963–1967) and the University of Michigan (~1968–1976), and later held a post at Indiana University from ~1977 to 2010.

Lynn Thomas is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She earned her BA and MA at Lancaster University and completed a D.Phil at Oxford in 1987, later lecturing in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton (attested 1997).

Léon Feer was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux. He held posts at INALCO, the Collège de France (1869–1872), and the Bibliothèque nationale de France starting in 1872.

Léon Vandermeersch was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy who studied in Paris. He held academic posts at the University of Provence (~1966–1973), Paris Diderot University (~1973–1979), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1979–1993).
M. D. Balasubrahmanyam was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967) and completed his dissertation there in 1969.
M. H. Krishna was an Indologist and historian who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1907–1911). He served as Professor of History at the University of Mysore (attested 1910).
